_comment: #3790 — cross-implementation cookie vectors. ONE artifact, TWO consumers:
the guard's Python verifier and the Clearing's TypeScript verifier both assert
against this file. DEC-2209 clause 2 asks for a shared verifier crate; until
#3685 delivers it there are two implementations of one contract, and drift
between them would surface as a login that works on one surface and not the
other. This turns that drift into a red test instead of a Tuesday outage.
The key here is a TEST key, named below, so the file stays committable.

vectors.name: valid
vectors.why: the happy path — without it every negative below passes against a verifier that refuses everything

vectors.name: tampered-mac
vectors.why: signature must be checked, in constant time

vectors.name: tampered-payload
vectors.why: a swapped identity with a stolen mac — the attack the signature exists for

vectors.name: missing-exp
vectors.why: a correctly-signed cookie with no expiry never expires; absent exp is a refusal, not a default

vectors.name: payload-not-json
vectors.why: signed garbage is still garbage — verify must not throw, it must refuse

vectors.name: mac-over-raw-json
vectors.why: THE TRAP: mac computed over the raw JSON instead of the base64url payload string. An implementation that makes this mistake rejects every real cookie AND accepts this one, so it is the single vector that catches the whole class.

vectors.name: no-separator
vectors.why: malformed input must refuse, never raise

vectors.name: empty
vectors.why: absent is not anonymous-but-fine; it is nobody
